newsitem.title: USA: Gilbert Associates says expects Q1 losses.
newsitem.headline: Gilbert Associates says expects Q1 losses.

text.p: Gilbert Associates said Wednesday it expects to report a loss from continuing operations of $0.10-$0.12 per share in the first fiscal quarter ended April 4 because its earnings of its telecommunications business will fall short of expectations.
The company said the April 4 reporting period is expected to be the first in which it it includes only its telecommunications segment in continuing operations.

The company said it appears the first quarter earnings performance of the telecommunications business will fall short of its expectations, primarily because of shortfalls in revenue in its wireless business.

Timothy Cobb, chairman and CEO of Gilbert, said: "The resulting shortfall in earnings comes despite healthy revenue growth and strong earnings results in both the industrial and wireless telecommunications business."
Cobb said the company therefore thought it was important to release a preliminary earnings annoucement rather than waiting for final results.
The company expects to report final earnings for the first quarter on April 30. It expects revenue in the range of $24 million to $25 million and losses of $650,000 to $750,000.
Consolidated net income, including discontinued operations, is expected to be in the range of $200,000 to $300,000, or $0.03 to $0.05 per share.

The company expects to adopt discontinued operations treatment for its technical services and real estate activities. The sale of these units should generate after-tax proceeds of $40 million to $60 million. In the same period last year, the company reported revenue of $20 million and net income from continuing operations of about $140,000, or $0.02 a share.
